        Frequently Asked Questions

        What are financial ratios and why are they important?

        Financial ratios are numerical tools derived from financial statements that help assess a company’s performance, liquidity, profitability, solvency, and efficiency. They allow comparison over time, across companies, and against industry benchmarks.

        What does gross profit margin indicate?

        It measures the efficiency of production. A higher margin means the company retains more per unit of sales.

        How is net profit margin different from operating margin?

        Net profit margin includes all expenses, including tax and interest. Operating margin only considers income from operations (EBIT).

        What is earnings per share (EPS)?

        It shows how much profit is earned per share — a key metric for investors.

        Why is return on equity (ROE) important?

        ROE shows how efficiently a company uses shareholders' funds.

        What does the current ratio show?

        It measures short-term liquidity. A ratio greater than 1 means the firm can meet its short-term obligations.

        What does return on assets (ROA) measure?

        ROA indicates how efficiently assets generate profit.

        What is the operating cash flow ratio?

        It assesses whether operating cash flows can cover short-term liabilities.

        What does the cash flow margin show?

        It reflects how effectively sales are converted into actual cash.

        How do financial ratios help investors?

        They provide a quick way to evaluate company performance, financial health, and risk, and to compare across peers or industry benchmarks.
